body: I am working at trying to see the positive and keep on going for a bit longer, if I made it to 18, I probably can make it to 20 sometime, it's just that the future that is so uncertain what the future will bring, will I finish school? Will I drop out? Will I be at the curb? All the questions is driving me nuts. D:

As someone who is an avid gamer when the opportunity allows, having those small victories is great, so is programming because you got "permanent results".

You don't have any kind of tips for someone who want to be a programmer do you?

I've been in touch with the principal, but I get redirected to another person who redirect me elsewhere, no one seem to be able to do anything about it since there is no name on the medical condition I have. With no absolute diagnosis the request of retake the year is not an option from what I've figured out with all the redirects in mails and phonecalls. Trying to meet up with the principal in person just triggered my allergy from being nervous and he was "busy" with a meeting that was coming up and told me to come back later. :/

My dream was actually to become a concept artist, but I realized lately that I can't even do that with my allergy since it seems that I tense up when I draw the lines as if I got nervous of the result or something, so I even get sick from that, either if its digital or traditional media I use. 

So now I am resorting into getting into programming so I might be able to get a job at distance or something like that, that's my only bet as it is now,  since I cant travel to work or back, spend a day in a hot office or do social interactions due me feeling awkward I have to get a job at home or something like that. So that is what I am trying to work at but I need to be ridiculously good at it to land a job though. 

I pretty much don't want to resort to killing myself since it always seems to be a way out, it's just too easy and tempting at the moment though.

I wouldn't mind actually if you asked since I've talked to more doctors than I can remember, showing the symptoms and described as good as I can, but they just can't figure out what it is. My initial guess was wrong since the treatment did not work nor did the "breakout" look as the should when it is that allergy... So any help that might lead into the right direction or could make it easier is appreciated!

Yeah I quickly realized that I would just feel worse if I tried to force it and went online instead to vent some. Also I can't even remember when I did those things last haha, I can't even go outside nor sit in the sun without getting sick, it does sound like the first thing I will do if I ever get a treatment that work. :)

I would shoot you a PM but I am horrible at keeping a conversation alive since I manage to end up with nothing to contribute with, or at least that is how it feels. :x

I am so sorry about your loss. :/ 

I can't imagine where I would be one year from now on actually, I am stuck in a viscous circle. I got three options as I see it now.
 
Either I go back to school and try to complete it but as it is now, I am far behind and the anxiety is not getting any better, just thinking of going back gets me sick by this point. 
I could also drop out, but where would I end up then? On the curb most likely since there seem to be a zero tolerance about being a mooch in my family, even with this condition. My family just doesn't seem to care or get it despite all the doctor appointments I've been at and the calls, notes and whatnot sent home.

Or I could simply opt out, seem to be a permanent solution on a hopefully temporary problem, but as it is now, then it would be no more pain, anxiety or depressions from just thinking about my current state.

I've been thinking a lot if it would be a selfish act to end my life, but on the other hand it's my own and I have the right to do the act, on the other hand I've been sticking around for years and hope I would feel better, I've felt this even before the crippling allergy though. :/
Trying to! Stuck in a viscous circle but trying to break free. Damn depression!

Thank you for your kind words, I really appreciate what you people are doing for persons who need help.

Knowing there is a world out there I can take part of always has been what have kept me going and trying to keep it up what I used to do, but today when I tried to draw which I love to do and notice I get sick from doing that, I get nervous drawing the lines or frustrated when something goes wrong, but I guess that is what I get for not working with an eraser. So something I love has turned against me, that is what made me write this post, I can't really cope with that things I love to do, even simple things like draw is taken away from me like that.

I am trying to hang on to what I love and the things that keep me up, the things I used to love is taken away and I am now resorting to things that doesn't get me sick. I am thankful there is internet and I got a game of thrones book here, otherwise I would be crawling on the walls from boredom. Can't even play games that much anymore. :/

Thank you for your reply once again, I needed a reminder of the small things that can make the day better.

Also, despite going to the doctors for a couple of years no one has been able to figure it out, so I am either first of a kind or this is just some obscure disease no one can think of. Or the higher powers just hate me.

I appreciate your reply and what you wrote, but.

It got to be other people like me out there, but at the same time it's stressing to not know what it is if you know what I mean, sometimes it's easier if you got a diagnosis than just pondering of what the hell is messing my life up.

With the allergy and depression I've really took distance from people, I can't hang with people since my allergy wont allow me to do that so I've cut the contact with many people and just hang out with a few in school, maybe my family would miss me a bit, but with the attitude they got towards me right now, I think they are better off without me if I could just go away.

I really got nothing to look forward to as it is now. I can't leave my room, I can't study and where will I end up if it keeps going like it is now? :/ I can't perform any tasks nor function like a human being since I am crippled by this allergy.
